notice.title: What's new
notice.text:
Four ways in

Four leads. Pick Xander Soren or Rue on the Spine, or Hicks or Ember in Karasu. Each still meets the others as a contact. Mother Rot and Ines leave the select screen: you find them through rumors and leads.

Make someone. + MAKE SOMEONE at 1P builds your own character: answer a few questions about body, face and clothes, generate a figure, fit it, and give them a name, pronouns and a past.

Soren's story. Three jobs with Rue, one at each tier, building a crew the branch doesn't know about. How it ends decides what's still open with Rue and with Kroll. Between jobs, Kroll's desk on the SDG floor has five more.

Ilse Kroll. Soren's handler is recast: same role, same secrets, a colder smile. She pours tea for the people she's buying and never drinks it.

Rue's side. Run Sheet, told from her side, is how Rue's game opens.

Hicks's cases. The Passenger opens a run of jobs with Ember in his ear, The Yes Book follows at tier 2, and House Glass puts him to work beside Nix.

Ember's opening. Signed, at the Tilt.

A story opening. A new game for a lead opens on their story's first scene. CUSTOM writes your own, SUGGEST deals three.

The intro. The game opens on a short story of the city and two of its runners, the names decrypting in block letters.

Graft, the job game

Jobs at a card table. Jobs are a tabletop-style game beside the chat, owing a lot to Blades in the Dark. Roll a handful of pixel d6: the highest die decides a clean pass, a pass at a cost, or a miss.

Go in your way. Pick QUIET, SMOOTH or HARD, up to three crew and your deck's programs, then play them as cards. Each way in shapes the trouble you get.

Choose your costs. A roll that goes partly wrong deals costs and you pick one, RESIST it with NERVE, or burn a FIREWALL. A roll lands SMALL, FAIR or BIG; trade with SAFE or BOLD, or PUSH.

Programs you own. Everyone starts with FIREWALL and one program for their best stat. Fixers sell the rest, and a job can drop a one-use foil.

Tiers bite. From tier 2 a roll lands a step smaller unless the right crew or deck covers it.

Press your luck. After the take, WALK with what you've got or PRESS ON for more.

Crew jobs. Some jobs drop the dice: each card says who can do it and what their way costs, and you send your people.

Boards. Some cases end on a board: lay the clue cards to name who, how and why, or tell two listeners two different stories without getting caught.

Contracts. Big jobs are gone. A contract is one contact's offer, crew groundwork over several nights, a long night on the table and fallout days later. They reach you as RUMORS once your rep has earned them.

Your contact rides along. On a job they answer your moves in a line or two, and when they're in your ear they stay in chat on comms.

Faces in the job. The people a job introduces appear beside the paragraph that brings them in.

Results stay on the table. Your rolls, what you keep and each crew member's fate stand on their cards, and the debrief says where your heat came from.

Tips. Your first jobs explain each piece the first time it matters. Rest on any card to see what it does now.

Crew

Abilities. Every recruit has them, GREEN to VET, once per job.

Vouches and rescues. Contacts who trust you vouch for a free hire, and SPRING THEM gets a held recruit out.

Goods. COLLECT fills a stash of four, HUSTLE sells it along a route, and each district wants one kind a night.

Fairer wages. You pay only for a night someone worked.

The story

The city moves without you. Every couple of story hours the contacts you're not with get on with their lives, and you may get a text about it. SYS → WORLD MOVES turns it off.

A contact hands you her job. Some jobs only open once a contact tells you about them, in person or by text.

The Residual. After every reply a quiet second pass keeps the Black Ledger: memory, standing, plans, promised texts, hidden truths for LOOSE ENDS, and the habits she should stop repeating.

People remember the scenes they were in. Talk to Silas with Ember in the room, and she knows about it later.

Shared plans. A meeting can name who else is coming, they turn up, and nobody invents a time.

DRAW deals three kinds. A STRANGER with a face, THE CITY acting, or something PERSONAL.

SUGGEST, three ways. Alt+G drafts PLAIN, PUSH and TURN.

Outfits you earn. Some open with trust and warmth, some are an ending's reward, and PEOPLE lets you pick what your contact wears.

Blackouts. Districts go dark on a schedule, and your room goes with them.

The new look

One red line. Every screen is redrawn as thin red trace over the room: YOU, PEOPLE, CREW, JOBS, the map, the pause menu and the chat box.

JOBS. QUEST is now JOBS, with HERE, ELSEWHERE, FIXER and RUMORS. Every job says who posted it. GO THERE walks you to it.

PEOPLE with TEXTS. Your contacts, their texts and your journal on one list.

The BOOK (Alt+B). The city's lore slides in beside the scene while you type, sorted, with corp logos and the city's customs.

The map's list. Places fold under their districts with who's there. The rendered city is relit and its seams are gone.

Room moves lose signal. GO and doors collapse like an old CRT, then the new room opens.

Lit figures. You and your contact take the room's lamps from every side, breathe, stand at their own height, and wear the room's grain.

Sound everywhere. New sounds for the panels, map, texts, jobs and menus, and every room has a bed under it.

Keys. Link NanoGPT or Anthropic beside OpenRouter.

Frame rate. The room draws at 60 by default. SYS → FRAME RATE sets 30, 60 or UNCAPPED.

Load in place. LOAD takes this game back to the save, and keeps where you were as BEFORE LOAD.

Open source. Lowlight's code is public under GPL-3.0, its content under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

Removed

Hack and slip. The gig board is papers only.

Paper Trail and Declared Dead. House Glass takes their place.

Fixes

GO WITH HER goes. You walk there together.

They answer as themselves. After a job a contact no longer speaks as you, and on comms knows what they heard, not what you saw.

Big lights reach. Some stopped in a hard circle in Chromium; they now light all they should.

Long lines show whole in the chat box.

Figures stay whole in a small Firefox window.

Sharper faces for crew, locals and Sentinels.

Loose ends keep coming through a long playthrough.

Every word on the top bar clicks.
